```
completion(prompt, model?="default"|"smol"|"slow", system?=None, schema?=None) → handle; `.wait()` returns text (parsed with `schema`). Stateless, no tools/history.
await judge(state, questions, images?=[path | ImageContent, …]) → `{id: answer}`
    Typed judgment over one `state` (str | JSON object | JSON array). Every question sees the same state and is answered independently: batch independent questions into one call. Cheap and fast (TypeSafe when credentialed, else the tiny/smol chat model); prefer over `completion()` for classification, yes/no, ranking. Two or more states → `judge_batch`, never a loop of `judge()`.
    `questions`: `{id: q}` where q is one of
      `{type: "choice", instructions, criteria: {label: rubric | None, …}}` → `{choice, probabilities: {label: p}, confidence}` (≥2 labels)
      `{type: "bool", instructions, criteria?: {true?: str, false?: str}}` → `{bool: P(yes)}`
      `{type: "score", instructions, criteria: [lowest, …, highest]}` → `{score, probabilities: {"0": p, …}, confidence}` (≥2 levels; score is the probability-weighted level index)
judge_batch(states, questions, concurrency?=32, retries?=1, min_ok?=1, intent?=None, images?={key: [path | ImageContent, …]}) → JudgmentBatch
    Images accept local paths or embedded `ImageContent`; batch attachments map each state key to its list (array inputs use zero-based index keys). Image requests skip candidates without image support, never silently drop images, and fail if no compatible judge remains.
    Same `questions` over every state (`{key: state}` or a list keyed by index), run and owned by the host — it outlives the cell. `intent` is an optional nonempty progress/job label (default `"Judging"`). Returns at once; pull settled items in bounded slices across cells: `await b.drain(timeout?)` → `[(key, item)]` settled since the last drain (`[]` on timeout; `item.answers` on success, else `item.error`, never raised); `async for k, item in b.drain_iter(timeout)` until timeout or completion; `b.status()` → `{intent, done, total, failed, cost, running, model}`; `b.results()` → `{key: answers}` so far; `b.failed()` → `{key: error}`; `b.cancel()`; `b.close()` releases it. `drain()` raises only when the run died wholesale (no judge, or fewer than `min_ok` answered). `b.id` is an async job id: completion auto-delivers a summary, `wait` blocks when you have nothing else to do, `judge_batch.attach(id)` re-creates the ref after a reset.
```
